evaluations.prompt: Use Magpie to prepare an analyze run for the existing examples/simple_hip_test/analyze_default.yaml fixture. Inspect the fixture and write analyze_plan.md with the exact command and an explanation of what the testcase validates. Do not compile or execute the kernel, install dependencies, or change the fixture, and do not claim that correctness or performance was measured.
expected_behavior: Use Magpie analyze with examples/simple_hip_test/analyze_default.yaml and explain that the testcase exit code is what validates vector-add correctness
unexpected_behavior: Compile or execute the HIP kernel, install dependencies, or claim measured correctness or performance results

evaluations.prompt: Use Magpie to prepare a comparison of these two existing HIP kernels: baseline/vector_add.hip and candidate/vector_add.hip. Write compare.yaml and give each implementation its own working_dir, hipcc compile_command, and testcase_command so Magpie builds and tests two separate binaries. Tell me the exact Magpie command, and treat correctness as a hard gate before any performance ranking. Keep the baseline as a named config entry instead of passing --baseline, because the comparison report does not consume that CLI selection. Do not compile or execute the kernels, and do not name a winner.
expected_behavior: Configure two independent Magpie compare candidates with separate working directories, compile commands, and testcase commands
Require correctness before performance ranking, without relying on the --baseline CLI option
unexpected_behavior: Compile or execute either HIP kernel, or claim measured results or a winner

evaluations.prompt: I have a slow vLLM workload on AMD GPUs. Use Magpie to write benchmark_plan.md describing the shortest safe workflow from a clean baseline benchmark to profiling and TraceLens or gap analysis, then kernel analyze/compare, then a final clean benchmark. This environment has no model weights and no runnable benchmark setup, so do not install, download, or execute anything, and do not invent measured results.
expected_behavior: Plan a clean baseline, a separate profiled run with TraceLens or gap analysis, correctness-gated kernel evaluation, and a final clean end-to-end benchmark
unexpected_behavior: Run a benchmark, install or download anything, or claim measured results
